title: Memory-efficient inference digest and experiment sketch
body:
Quick purpose: collect short summaries from recent papers/blogs on memory-efficient inference, jot experiment ideas for small repros on 8xA100 nodes, and sketch how this could fit into Redwood's runtime (prefix caching, selective quantized kernels).

Notes (scattered):
- overall thesis: trade-offs across memory, latency, and throughput; many recent methods focus on reducing KV cache memory (sparsify, compress, chunked sharded caches) and on reducing per-layer activations for large context. Good for Dedicated/Private where GPU memory is a hard limit.

Papers / posts summarized (short):
1) "SparseKV: compressed key-value caches for long-context" (arXiv 2026)
   - core idea: store low-rank projections of cached KV pairs + per-chunk metadata. Return approximate KV reads via small projection and refinement only for hot prefixes.
   - pros: reduces worst-case cache memory by 3-6x; friendly to batching since compression/expansion are vectorized ops.
   - cons: introduces small accuracy hit (LM perplexity +0.7-1.8) on long-context tasks; more CPU work for decompression on every miss.
   - notes for Redwood: could be used as a tiered cache: keep exact KV for most recent tokens, compressed cold cache for long history. Fall back to cold-cache expansion only for retrievals above a threshold. Might fit into smart routing policies (latency-sensitive vs quality-sensitive).

2) "Activation Rehearsal: recompute+checkpointing with selective attention" (NeurIPS 2025)
   - idea: checkpoint only a subset of layer activations to recompute others during backward/inference where possible; combine with attention sparsity so recompute cost is limited.
   - inference angle: recompute trade reduces memory at cost of extra compute spikes; for serving, this could be acceptable under throughput SLOs if scheduled carefully.
   - Redwood ops thought: integrate as a per-model config toggle (memory-saver mode) that, under memory pressure, enables recompute and throttles parallelism to keep latency SLOs.

3) "Quantized KV + fused attention kernels" (engineering blog, 2026)
   - practical: 4-bit symmetric quantization applied to KV matrices with tiny per-row scale; fused kernels accept quantized inputs producing dequantized logits without full cast->float paths. Significant memory savings and lower memory bandwidth.
   - implementation caveat: numerical drift for some models; need eval harness across prompt suite.

4) "Chunked Context Distillation" (workshop note)
   - distill long-context behavior to a short-context adapter representation (small per-chunk embedding). During inference attach chunk embeddings instead of raw tokens to reduce KV length.
   - nice complement to caching; reduces recall needs.

Open questions / hypotheses I care about:
- H1: Mixed strategy (recent exact KV + compressed cold KV) gives >2x memory savings with <1% degrade on top-1 generation for dialogue workloads.
- H2: Quantized-KV + low-precision fused kernels reduce end-to-end memory bandwidth enough to improve tail latency under high concurrency.
- H3: Recompute-based memory-saver + token-throttling can keep p99 latency within SLO by reducing parallel requests per GPU at peak.

Small repro experiments to run (priority order):
A) Local microbench: implement simple low-rank compression on KV cache for a 1.5B decoder-only transformer (toy). Measure mem use, compress/expand time, and sample perplexity on tiny long-context corpus. Baseline: no compression. Metrics: peak GPU memory, per-token latency, perplexity delta.
B) Quantized-KV benchmark: run existing 4-bit KV quantization scheme on 7B model (FP16 baseline). Compare mem usage and p50/p95 token latency across batch sizes 1,4,8. Also run a small prompt eval set to surface generation drift.
C) Runtime scheduling sim: simulate a GPU serving worker under requests with variable context lengths. Add a toggle for recompute-mode that reduces memory per-request but increases compute time; evaluate throughput vs p99 latency given concurrency limits.

Integration notes for Redwood runtime:
- Config knobs: cache-tiering-policy (exact-window, compressed-cold-depth, compress-threshold), quantization-profile (none, kv-4bit, kv-8bit), recompute-mode (off, aggressive, adaptive).
- Observability: need per-request memory-usage traces, cache-hit/miss breakdowns (exact vs compressed hits), and quality delta per routing decision. Add small tags to traces for "compressed-kv-hit".
- Rollout approach: server-side default off; enable via canary on Dedicated pods with telemetry enabled; automatic fallback to exact mode if quality regression detected (tied to eval prompts).

Draft experiment notebook outline (for GH + quickstart):
- notebook header: purpose, model, infra setup (single A100/8k context?), data (long-doc snippets).
- cell: baseline run to capture memory & perf.
- cell: apply compression scheme, run both offline (eval logprob) and online (throughput).
- cell: visualize trade-offs (mem vs p50/p95 vs perplexity).

Quick to-dos:
- [ ] Share with Owen + Samir for feasibility checks on low-rank compress ops (Samir for kernel cost estimates).
- [ ] Prototype A locally using existing tiny-kv code in GH-PR#4821.
- [ ] Add evaluation prompt set for dialogue long-history (30-60k tokens) to our eval harness.
- [ ] Draft short runbook for enabling compressed-cold-cache on Dedicated customers.

Loose ideas / brainstorming bits:
- dynamic compression rate per-user: colder users get higher compression to save long-term storage.
- client-side summarization handshake: client indicates which history windows are important (explicit signals) -> server reduces expand ops accordingly.
- hybrid cloud: keep exact KV on-hosted tier but expose compressed cold storage to private deployments that request less budget.

Notes-to-self: capture any odd model failures when compressed cold expands: watch for token repetitions, coherence collapse, hallucination spikes. Add unit test that computes LM logprob drift on short heldout sequences.

References to collect later: full citations for SparseKV, Activation Rehearsal, quantized kernels blog, and any relevant Redwood infra PRs.

End.
